thought.text: Race reproduced: 50 concurrent increments all read 0 before any write, so the final count is 1. The fix is to guard only the tiny read-modify-write critical section with an `asyncio.Lock`, keeping the simulated work (the `sleep`) concurrent — locking the whole body would serialize the 30 × 0.005s sleeps (~0.15s) and blow the 0.08s concurrency budget.

reasoning_content:
Race confirmed: 50 concurrent increments all read 0, then all write 1 → count is 1 not 50.

Now implement the fix: guard only the read-modify-write with an asyncio.Lock, keeping the simulated work (the sleep) concurrent.

action.old_str:
class AsyncCounter:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.value = 0

    async def increment(self) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(WORK_DELAY_SECONDS)
        current = self.value
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        self.value = current + 1
action.new_str:
class AsyncCounter:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.value = 0
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def increment(self) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(WORK_DELAY_SECONDS)
        async with self._lock:
            current = self.value
            self.value = current + 1
